21895.text: A person writes four letters and address four envelopes. If the letters are placed in the envelopes at random, then the probability that not all letters are placed in the right envelope is
21895.sol: The total number of ways to place 4 letters into 4 envelopes is 4! = 24 . The event that all letters are placed in the right envelope corresponds to exactly 1 way (each letter in its corresponding envelope). The probability that all letters are placed in the right envelope is P(A) = 1 24 . The probability that not all letters are placed in the right envelope is the complement of the event that all letters are placed correctly. Therefore, the required probability is 1 - P(A) = 1 - 1 24 = 23 24 . Answer: 23 24

32222.subject: Chemistry
32222.text: Given below are two statements: Statement-I: The orbitals having same energy are called as degenerate orbitals. Statement-II: In hydrogen atom, 3 p and 3 d orbitals are not degenerate orbitals. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given
options: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
32222.sol: Degenerate orbitals are the orbitals of the same subshell having equal energies. When the electrons of the orbitals are not influenced by any external factors like an electric field or magnetic field, they have same energies. For a single electron species like hydrogen atom, the energy depends upon the principal quantum number ' n ' only. Hence, 3 s , 3 p and 3 d oribitals have same energy. So, statement II is false. Statement I is correct definition of degenerate orbitals. Hence, the answer is option A.

Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
70895.sol: Statement I is incorrect because gemmules are internal buds formed for asexual reproduction in sponges (phylum Porifera), not in coelenterates. Coelenterates typically reproduce asexually through external budding. Statement II is incorrect because a gemmule consists of a central mass of totipotent cells called archaeocytes, which are responsible for developing into a new sponge. 71400.subject: Biology
71400.text: Which of the following term is best suited for the process, which involves production of offsprings by the formation and fusion of gametes?
71400.sol: Amphimixis is the process of sexual reproduction which involves the formation and fusion of male and female gametes to produce offspring. Apomixis is a type of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction but occurs without the fusion of gametes. Apogamy is the development of a sporophyte directly from a gametophyte without fertilization. Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilization, resulting in seedless fruits. Answer: Amphimixis

71417.subject: Biology
71417.text: Diosgenin is primarily used in the manufacturing of------
71417.sol: Diosgenin is a phytosteroid sapogenin extracted from the tubers of Dioscorea species (wild yam). It serves as a crucial precursor for the semi-synthesis of various steroid hormones, most notably progesterone. Progesterone and its derivatives are key active ingredients in oral contraceptives. Therefore, diosgenin is primarily used in the manufacturing of birth control pills. Answer: birth control pills

options: A, B, C, D and E

79554.sol: R.H. Whittaker (1969) proposed the Five Kingdom Classification. The main criteria used by him for this classification include: 1. Cell structure (prokaryotic or eukaryotic) 2. 79890.subject: Botany
79890.text: A somatic cell that has just completed the S phase of its cell cycle, as compared to gamete of the same species, has:
options: Twice the number of chromosomes and twice the amount of DNA
Same number of chromosomes but twice the amount of DNA
Twice the number of chromosomes and four times the amount of DNA
Four times the number of chromosomes and twice the amount of DNA
79890.sol: S-phase (synthesis phase) is the part of the cell cycle in which DNA is replicated, but a number of chromosome does not change. If a cell is diploid then after S phase DNA content in the cell will be 4 C and Chromosome in the cell will be 2 N. While in a gamete, DNA content in gamete = C Chromosome in gamete = N Hence, the Number of chromosome in a somatic cell will be twice than gamete while DNA content will be four times.

83068.text: Water rises to a height 'h' in capillary tube. If the length of capillary tube above the surface of water is made less than 'h', then:
options: water rises upto the top of capillary tube and stays there without overflowing.
water rises upto a point a little below the top and stays there.
water does not rise at all.
water rises upto the tip of capillary tube and then starts overflowing like a fountain.
83068.sol: It won't overflow. That should be obvious since doing so would create a constant flow, constantly using energy, but without any energy input. The same force that pulls the water along the inside of the capillary tube also holds it there when it reaches the end. This force doesn't just pull upward, it pulls the water along the glass. At a certain height, the weight of the water column balances this pull. In that case the pull is upward since there is water below but not above.

116682.sol: The tetrahedral [MO 4 ]n- ions are known for V, Cr, Mn, Mn, and Mn.

117371.subject: Chemistry
117371.text: Which type of ligand can bind through two donor atoms?
117371.sol: Didendate ligands can bind to a metal ion through two donor atoms.

117865.subject: Chemistry
117865.text: Which of the following is not considered as an organometallic compound?
117865.sol: is not an organometallic compound as it does not contain carbon-metal bond. Cisplatin is an inorganic compound, used as an anticancer drug and falls into class of DNA damaging agents.

118421.subject: Chemistry
118421.text: What is the main difference between the products of dehydrogenation and dehydration of alcohols?
options: Dehydrogenation forms aldehydes, while dehydration forms ketones.
Dehydrogenation forms alkenes, while dehydration forms alkanes.
Dehydrogenation forms ketones, while dehydration forms alkenes.
Dehydrogenation forms alkenes, while dehydration forms aldehydes.
118421.sol: The main difference is that dehydrogenation forms alkenes, while dehydration forms aldehydes.

118531.subject: Chemistry
118531.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding the solubility of phenols in water?
options: Solubility increases with the size of the alkyl groups.
Solubility decreases as the number of hydroxyl groups increases.
Solubility decreases with increased branching in the phenolic ring.
Solubility remains constant regardless of structural modifications.
118531.sol: Increased branching in the phenolic ring reduces the availability of -OH groups for hydrogen bonding with water, decreasing solubility.

118616.subject: Chemistry
118616.text: Match the chemical conversions in List I with the appropriate reagents in List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists : List - I List - II (A) (P) i Hg OAc 2 ; ii NaBH 4 (B) ​ (Q) NaOEt (C) (R) Et - Br (D) (S) i BH 3 ; ii H 2 O 2 / NaOH
118616.sol: A tertiary alkyl halide with strong base undergoes elimination reaction, while a primary alkyl halide with t - butoxide gives ether by a substitution reaction. Alkenes undergo hydration (addition of water) by Hydroboration-Oxidation, giving anti-Markovnikov's products and by Oxymercuration-Demercuration, giving Markovnikov's products.

118934.subject: Chemistry
118934.text: Which of the following is the correct sequence of step involved in the mechanism of Cannizzaro reaction?
options: Nucleophilic attack, transfer of H ⁻ and transfer of H ⁺
Transfer of H ⁻ , transfer of H ⁺ and nucleophilic attack
Transfer of H ⁺ , nucleophilic attack and transfer of H ⁻
Electrophilic attack by OH ⁻ , transfer of H ⁺ and transfer of H ⁻
118934.sol: Cannizzaro reaction involves the aldehydes which do not have an -hydrogen atom, undergo self oxidation and reduction reaction on heating with conc. alkali. HCHO + HCHO conc. KOH CH ₃ OH + HCOO ⁻ Mechanism Step I Attack of nucleophile OH ⁻ to the carbonyl carbon. Step II Transfer of hydride ion from anion I to second molecule of aldehyde and finally rapid transfer of proton takes place.

119088.subject: Chemistry
119088.text: How does steric hindrance affect the reactivity of aldehydes and ketones in nucleophilic addition reactions?
options: It increases reactivity in aldehydes and ketones
It decreases reactivity in aldehydes and ketones
It has no effect on reactivity
119088.sol: Sterically, the presence of two relatively large substituents in ketones hinders the approach of a nucleophile to the carbonyl carbon, reducing their reactivity compared to aldehydes.

119143.subject: Chemistry
119143.text: Would you expect benzaldehyde to be more reactive or less reactive in nucleophilic addition reactions than propanal? Explain your answer
options: Benzaldehyde would be more reactive because it has a stronger electron-donating group attached to the benzene
Benzaldehyde would be less reactive because it is more sterically hindered than propanal.
Benzaldehyde would be more reactive because it has a partially positive charge on the carbonyl carbon.
The carbon atom of the carbonyl group of benzaldehyde is less electrophilic than the carbon atom of the carbon
119143.sol: Correct Option is : (D) The carbon atom of the carbonyl group of benzaldehyde is less electrophilic than the carbon atom of the carbonyl group present in propanal. The polarity of the carbonyl group is reduced in benzaldehyde due to resonance and hence it is less reactive than propanal.

120367.subject: Chemistry
120367.text: What effect does histamine have on the muscles in the walls of fine blood vessels?
options: It has no effect on them.
120367.sol: Histamine relaxes the muscles in the walls of fine blood vessels.

120493.subject: Chemistry
120493.text: Assertion : Cimetidine is an antacid. Reason : Antacid increases secretion of HCl from gastric cells.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
120493.sol: Cimetidine is an antacid which suppresses the secretion of HCl .

120765.subject: Chemistry
120765.text: What is the role of the hydroxyl group at C-5 in glucose's ring formation?
options: It forms a hemiacetal with the aldehyde group.
It is responsible for reducing properties.
120765.sol: The hydroxyl group at C-5 is involved in ring formation when glucose undergoes cyclization.

121148.subject: Botany
121148.text: In biological terminology, a group of similar organisms which are capable of interbreeding and producing fertile offsprings is called
121148.sol: .The members of the same species can interbreed and produce fertile offspring. Taxonomic studies consider a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities as a species. One should be able to distinguish one species from the other closely related species based on the distinct morphological differences. Let us consider Mangifera indica, Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Panthera leo (lion). All the three names, indica, tuberosum and leo, represent the specific epithets, while the first words Mangifera, Sola

121344.subject: Botany
121344.text: What type of organism are Ascomycetes generally?
121344.sol: Commonly known as sac-fungi, the ascomycetes are mostly multicellular, e.g., Penicillium, or rarelyunicellular, e.g., yeast (Saccharomyces). They are saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous (growing on dung). Mycelium is branched and septate. The asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores. Conidia on germination produce mycelium. Sexual spores are called ascosporeswhich are produced endogenously in sac like asci (singular ascus). These asci are arranged

121506.subject: Botany
121506.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Members of kingdom Animalia are autotrophic 2. Kingdom Animalia members have a holozoic mode of nutrition 3. Members of kingdom Animalia are multicellular and possess a cell wall 4. animals store food reserves as protein.
121506.sol: Members of Kingdom Animalia digest their food in an internal cavity and store food reserves as glycogen or fat. Their mode of nutrition is holozoic – by ingestion of food.

121766.subject: Botany
121766.text: How are bryophytes attached to the substratum?
121766.sol: Bryophytes include the various mosses and liverworts that are found commonly growing in moist shaded areas in the hills. Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction. They usually occur in damp, humid and shaded localities. They play an important role in plant succession on bare rocks/soil. The plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attach

121847.subject: Botany
121847.text: What type of plant group do angiosperms represent?
121847.sol: Unlike the gymnosperms where the ovules are naked, in the angiosperms or flowering plants, the pollen grains and ovules are developed in specialized structures called flowers. In angiosperms, the seeds are enclosed in fruits. The angiosperms are an exceptionally large group of plants occurring in a wide range of habitats. They range in size from the smallest Wolffia to tall trees of Eucalyptus (over 100 meters). They provide us with food, fodder, fuel, medicines and several other commercially important products. Th

121973.subject: Botany
121973.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The common forms are Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra and Chara. 2. The members of Rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. 3. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas. 4. They occur in only well-lighted regions clo
121973.sol: The common forms of phaeophyceae are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus. The members of Rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas.

122159.subject: Botany
122159.text: Which of the following is/are grouped under phanerogams?
122159.sol: Eichler (1883) divided plant kingdom into two sub-kingdoms. (i) Cryptogamae- Plants having no flowers such as algae, fungi, bryophytes and pteridophytes (ii) Phanerogamae- Plants having evident reproductive organs like flowers and seeds such as angiosperms and gymnosperms.

122183.subject: Botany
122183.text: What level of cellular organization is exhibited by animals such as Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs, and Chordates?
122183.sol: Though all members of Animalia are multicellular, all of them do not exhibit the same pattern of organisation of cells. For example, in sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, i.e., they exhibit cellular level of organisation. Some division of labour (activities) occur among the cells. In coelenterates, the arrangement of cells is more complex. Here the cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, hence is called tissue level of organisation. A still higher level of organisation,

122185.subject: Botany
122185.text: What type of symmetry do sponges have?
122185.sol: Animals can be categorised on the basis of their symmetry. Sponges are mostly asymmetrical, i.e., any plane that passes through the centre does not divide them into equal halves. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. Coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms have this kind of body plan. Animals like annelids, arthropods, etc., where the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, exhi

122213.subject: Botany
122213.text: What is the body shape of Aschelminthes?
122213.sol: The body of Aschelminthes is circular in cross-section, hence the name roundworms. Aschelminthes may be freeliving, aquatic and terrestrial or parasitic in plants and animals. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.Fertilization is internal in Aschelminthes.They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and pseudocoelomate animals. Alimentary canal is complete with a well- developed muscular pharynx. An excretory tube removes body wastes from the body cavity through the excretory pore. Sexes are s

122306.subject: Botany
122306.text: What is the other name of this organism?

122452.subject: Botany
122452.text: Water transport system Phylum A. Minute pores (ostia) to central cavity (spongocoel) to osculum 1. Sponges B. Gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening 2. Ctenophores C. Central cavity with ciliated comb plates 3. Cnidarians D. Absorption through body surface 4. Platyhelminthes
122452.sol: Sponges use a water transport system with ostia, spongocoel, and osculum. Cnidarians have a gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening. Ctenophores have central cavities with comb plates. Platyhelminthes absorb nutrients through their body surface.

122589.subject: Botany
122589.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) Choanocytes (I) Ctenophora - Locomotion (B) Comb plates (II) Platyhelminthes - Osmoregulation and excretion (C) Flame cells (III) Porifera - Line the spongocoel and canals (D) Radula (IV) Mollusca - Feeding Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
122589.sol: (A) Choanocytes (collar cells) line the spongocoel and the canals in members of Phylum Porifera. (B) Comb plates are eight external rows of ciliated structures present in Ctenophores, which help in locomotion. (C) Flame cells are specialized cells in Platyhelminthes (flatworms) that help in osmoregulation and excretion. (D) Radula is a file-like rasping organ present in the mouth of Molluscs, used for feeding. Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), and (D)-(IV). Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I),

122838.subject: Botany
122838.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The primary roots and its branches constitute the tap root system. Reason: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short live and is replaced by a large number of roots.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
122838.sol: The primary roots and its branches constitute the tap root system. In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short lived and is replaced by a large number of roots.

123183.subject: Botany
123183.text: Expanded green stem of Opuntia is called
123183.sol: Phylloclade is a modified stem or branch which may be flat or circular, fleshy, like green leaf, eg, Opuntia.

123477.subject: Botany
123477.text: The branched sclereids present in hydrophytes
123477.sol: Sclereids are highly thickened dead sclerenchyma cells with very narrow cavities. They may also be branched. They provide stiffness to the parts in which they occur. Sclereids are of many types: brachysclereids, macrosclereids, osteosclereids, astrosclereids, trichosclereids and filiform sclereids. Astrosclereids are star-shaped, having various branches or arms. They are found in intercellular spaces of leaves and stems of many hydrophytes like Nymphaea.

123702.subject: Botany
123702.text: What happens to the chromosomes during Telophase I?
options: The chromosomes reach the extremely extended state of the interphase nucleus
The chromosomes align on the equatorial plate
The chromosomes remain associated at their centromeres
123702.sol: Telophase I: The nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear, cytokinesis follows and this is called as dyad of Although in many cases the chromosomes do undergo some dispersion , they do not reach the extremely extended state of the interphase nucleus during Telophase I. The stage between the two meiotic divisions is called interkinesis and is generally short lived. There is no replication of DNA during interkinesis. Interkinesis is followed by prophase II, a much simpler prophase than prophase I.

123786.subject: Botany
123786.text: Meiosis in diploid organisms results in
options: Reduction in the number of chromosomes
123786.sol: Meiosis in diploid organisms results in production of gametes, reduction in the number of chromosomes and introduction of variation.

123918.subject: Botany
123918.text: Assertion : Meiosis II is similar to mitosis. Reason : Meiosis I cannot occur in haploid cells.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
123918.sol: Meiosis consists of two divisions, meiosis I and meiosis II. The first division of meiosis is called heterotypic or reduction division. During this division the number of chromosomes is reduced to half. The two chromatids of a chromosome become genetically different due to crossing over. These chromatids are separated in the second division of meiosis. The second meiotic division is known as homotypic or equational division, because the chromosome number remains the same as produced after the end of the first divis

124044.subject: Botany
124044.text: What is the composition of ribosomes?
124044.sol: Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953). They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane

124063.subject: Botany
124063.text: What are the structures that form the nuclear pores in the cell?
124063.sol: Explanation : At a number of places the nuclear envelope is interrupted by minute pores , which are formed by the fusion of its two membranes. These nuclear pores are the passages through which movement of RNA and protein molecules takes place in both directions between the nucleus and the cytoplasm..

124503.subject: Botany
124503.text: In the formula Lt = L0 + rt, what does ‘Lt’ represent?
124503.sol: On plotting the length of the organ against time, a linear curve is obtained. Mathematically, it is expressed as Lt = L0 + rt Lt = length at time ‘t’ L0 = length at time ‘zero’ r = growth rate / elongation per unit time.

124616.subject: Botany
124616.text: What is depicted in the X and Y axis?
options: X axis- Height of plant Y axis- Time
X axis- Time Y axis Height of plant
X axis- Time Y axis- Weight of plant

124901.subject: Botany
124901.text: The most important force which pulls water up in tall trees is :
124901.sol: The most important force which pulls water up in the tall trees is the cohesive (inter-molecular) force between H ₂ O molecules. It also helps in maintaining the continuity of water column in tall trees.

125136.subject: Botany
125136.text: Substrate Breakdown and Entry Points Respiratory Pathway Entry Points A. Fats 1. Broken down into glycerol and fatty acids; enters pathway as PGAL or acetyl CoA. B. Fatty Acids 2. Degraded to acetyl CoA and enters the Krebs cycle. C. Proteins 3. Degraded by proteases into amino acids; enters as pyruvate, acetyl CoA, or directly into the Krebs cycle. D. Glycerol 4. Converted into PGAL before entering the glycolytic pa
125136.sol: A - 4: Glycerol is converted into PGAL before entering the glycolytic pathway. B - 2: Fatty acids are degraded to acetyl CoA before entering the Krebs cycle. C - 3: Proteins are degraded into amino acids, which enter the pathway as pyruvate, acetyl CoA, or directly into the Krebs cycle. D - 1: Fats are broken down into glycerol and fatty acids; they enter the respiratory pathway as PGAL or acetyl CoA.

125207.subject: Botany
125207.text: Assertion : Glycolysis is the first step of respiration in which glucose completely breaks into CO ₂ and H ₂ O . Reason : In this process, there is net gain of twenty four molecules of ATP.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
125207.sol: Glycolysis is the process of breakdown of glucose or similar hexose sugar into two molecules of pyruvic acid through a series of enzyme mediated reactions, releasing energy (ATP) and reducing power ( NADH ₂ ) . It is the first step of respiration, which occurs inside the cytoplasm and is independent of O ₂ . In glycolysis, two molecules of ATP are consumed during double phosphorylation of glucose to form fructose 1, 6 diphosphate. Four molecules of ATP are produced in the conversion of 1,3-diphosphoglycerate to 3-p

125222.subject: Botany
125222.text: Phase common in aerobic and anaerobic respiration is
125222.sol: Glycolysis is an essential and first path of respiration. It is common in both aerobic and anaerobic respiration and occurs in the cytosol of all living cells of prokaryotes as well as eukaryotes.

125603.subject: Botany
125603.text: A C₃ plant is exposed to high temperature and high light intensity, leading to the closure of its stomata. Under these conditions, what will RuBisCO primarily bind to, and what are the immediate products formed in the reaction?
options: O ₂ ; one molecule of phosphoglycerate and one molecule of phosphoglycolate
CO ₂ ; two molecules of phosphoglycerate
O ₂ ; two molecules of phosphoglycolate
CO ₂ ; one molecule of oxaloacetic acid
125603.sol: Under high temperature and high light intensity, the stomata of C₃ plants close to prevent water loss. This stops the entry of atmospheric CO ₂ , while O ₂ continues to accumulate inside the leaf due to the ongoing photolysis of water in the light reactions. Because the binding of CO ₂ and O ₂ to the active site of RuBisCO is competitive, the high O ₂ to CO ₂ ratio forces the enzyme to function primarily as an oxygenase. In this photorespiratory pathway, RuBisCO binds O ₂ to RuBP (a 5-carbon compound), splitting it

125606.subject: Botany
125606.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In C₃ plants, some O ₂ binds to RuBisCO, resulting in a decrease in CO ₂ fixation. Reason (R): RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for O ₂ than for CO ₂ . In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
125606.sol: Assertion (A) is true: In C₃ plants, RuBisCO can bind to O ₂ instead of CO ₂ due to its dual catalytic nature. When O ₂ binds to RuBisCO, the wasteful process of photorespiration is initiated, which utilizes ATP and releases CO ₂ without synthesizing sugars, thereby decreasing the overall CO ₂ fixation. Reason (R) is false: According to NCERT, RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for CO ₂ than for O ₂ . The binding of these gases is competitive, and it is the relative concentration of O ₂ and CO ₂ at the active site

125705.subject: Botany
125705.text: Assertion : Due to pollution atmospheric concentration of CO ₂ is increasing which will be harmful for C ₄ plants whereas productivity is going to increase for C ₃ plants. Reason : C ₄ plants have greater efficiency for CO ₂ as CO ₂ is fixed by PEP oxygenase.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
125705.sol: CO ₂ concentration of the atmosphere is 0.036 % or 360 ppm (360 l . l⁻¹ ) . It is a limiting factor for C ₃ plants as the available CO ₂ concentration is lower than the optimum for photosynthesis. Increase in its concentration upto 0.05 % increases the rate of photosynthesis in most C ₃ plants. When CO ₂ concentration is reduced, there comes a point at which illuminated plant parts stop absorbing carbon dioxide from their environment. It is known as CO ₂ compensation point or threshold value. At this value CO ₂ fix

125832.subject: Botany
125832.text: In recent years, what has become a fashion in terms of pollen use?
options: Using pollen tablets as food supplements
125832.sol: Pollen grains of many species cause severe allergies and bronchial afflictions in some people often leading to chronic respiratory disorders– asthma, bronchitis, etc. It may be mentioned that Parthenium or carrot grass that came into India as a contaminant with imported wheat, has become ubiquitous in occurrence and causes pollen allergy. Pollen grains are rich in nutrients. It has become a fashion in recent years to use pollen tablets as food supplements. In western countries, a large number of pollen products in

126953.subject: Botany
126953.text: What will happen if fresh water lake gets contaminated by addition of polluted water with high BOD?
options: Number of submerged aquatic plants in the lake will increase
Number of aquatic animals in the lake will increase
Amount of dissolved oxygen in the lake will decrease
126953.sol: Higher BOD of water indicates higher amount of biodegradable organic materials present in it. Since BOD is inversely proportional to the dissolved oxygen (DO), therefore, the dissolved oxygen in the lake will decrease.

126981.subject: Botany
126981.text: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below: Column – I Column –II a. Eutrophication i. UV-B radiation b. Sanitary landfill ii. Deforestation c. Snow blindness iii. Nutrient d. Jhum cultivation iv. Waste disposal
options: a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
a - i, b -iii, c - iv, d - ii
a - ii, b - i, c - iii, d - iv
a - i, b - ii, c - iv, d - iii
126981.sol: Eutrophication is the nutrient enrichment of water bodies containing an excessive population of phytoplankton. This leads to an overgrowth of flora and fauna in the water body until the organic deposition makes it warmer and shallower. Warm-water population increases and the final stage is its conversion into a land. Sanitary Landfill is a method of solid waste disposal in which the waste material is buried in the pits dug on the ground and later they get covered by soil. Snow blindness is caused due to UV-B radiat

127532.subject: Botany
127532.text: The map given below indicates the former and the present distribution of an animal: Which animal could it be:
127532.sol: The wild ass, once widely distributed in north-western arid zone; now confined to Runn of Kutchehh and Pakistan.

127830.subject: Botany
127830.text: In an ecosystem, the total incident solar radiation is 2,000,000 J . The plants capture 1 % of this incident solar energy to form Gross Primary Productivity (GPP). If the respiratory loss (R) in plants is 20 % of their GPP, what amount of energy will be available to the secondary consumers?
127830.sol: Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is the total energy captured by plants. Here, it is 1 % of the incident solar radiation. GPP = 1 % of 2,000,000 J = 20,000 J Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the energy remaining after respiratory losses (R). R = 20 % of 20,000 J = 4,000 J NPP = GPP - R = 20,000 J - 4,000 J = 16,000 J The NPP is the energy available to the primary consumers (2nd trophic level). According to the 10% law, the energy available to the secondary consumers (3rd trophic level) will be 10% of the energy av

128026.subject: Zoology
128026.text: Which of the following is true regarding female reproductive system in frog
options: Consist of a pair of ovary, situated near kidney and functionally connected to kidneys
A pair of oviduct opens into cloaca separately and female lays 25000-30000 at once
Fertilisation is external and takes place in water
There is no such larval stage
128026.sol: The female reproductive organs include a pair of ovaries. The ovaries are situated near kidneys and there is no functional connection with kidneys. A pair of oviduct arising from the ovaries opens into the cloaca separately. A mature female can lay 2500 to 3000 ova at a time. Fertilisation is external and takes place in water. Development involves a larval stage called tadpole. Tadpole undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.

128378.subject: Zoology
128378.text: What are the effects of androgens on male individuals?
options: Stimulation of female secondary sex organs
128378.sol: Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the male accessory sex organs like epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate gland, urethra etc. These hormones stimulate muscular growth, growth of facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness, low pitch of voice etc. Androgens play a major stimulatory role in the process of spermatogenesis (formation of spermatozoa). Androgens act on the central neural system and influence the male sexual behaviour (libido). These hormones produce anabolic (sy

128460.subject: Zoology
128460.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate Reason: Thyroid hormones also support the process of white blood cell formation
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128460.sol: Thyroid hormones play an important role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate. Thyroid hormones also support the process of red blood cell formation

Exophthalmic goitre is a form of hypothyroidism characterised by protruding eyeballs. C. Diabetes mellitus is associated with loss of glucose through urine. D. Tetany is rapid spasm in muscle due to high Ca ⁺⁺ in body fluid. E. Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes defective developm
128598.sol: Statement A is correct as hypersecretion of growth hormone in adults causes acromegaly, which can lead to severe complications and premature death. Statement B is incorrect because exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is a form of hyperthyroidism, not hypothyroidism. Statement C is correct as prolonged hyperglycemia in diabetes mellitus leads to loss of glucose through urine. Statement D is incorrect because tetany is caused by low Ca ⁺⁺ levels in body fluid, not high. Statement E is correct as hypothyroidism duri

128672.subject: Zoology
128672.text: Endemic goitre is a state of
128672.sol: Goitre is a swelling of the neck due to enlargement of the thyroid gland. This may be due to lack of dietary iodine, which occurs due to decreases thyroid function, which is necessary for the production of thyroxine hormone. This was the cause of endemic goitre, formerly common in regions, where the people lacked in their diet iodine.

128757.subject: Zoology
128757.text: In the wall of alimentary canal, what is the actual sequence from outer to inner
options: serosa, long muscle, circular, submucosa, mucosa
128757.sol: The wall of alimentary canal is made up of four basic layers. Ist of all there is serosa which is a thin membranous covering around oesophagus. Then there is muscle layer-outer layer of longitudinal muscles and inner layer of circular muscles. Last there is submucosa, which contains a few oesophageal glands. Then comes mucosa, which have several layers of flattened cells.

128844.subject: Zoology
128844.text: What is the function of the closed circulatory system?
128844.sol: The circulatory patterns are of two types – open or closed. Open circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs in which blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities called sinuses. Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system in which the blood pumped by the heart is always circulated through a closed network of blood vessels. This pattern is considered to be more advantageous as the flow of fluid can be more precisely regulated.

129154.subject: Zoology
129154.text: The blood group with antibody-a and antibody-b is
129154.sol: Persons having blood group-O have no antigens but have both anibodies a and b in their plasma.

129178.subject: Zoology
129178.text: What is the neural system of all animals composed of?
129178.sol: Coordination refers to the process by which two or more organs interact and complement each other's functions in order to maintain homeostasis. The neural system of all animals is composed of highly specialized cells called neurons, which can detect, receive, and transmit different kinds of stimuli. The neural organization is very simple in lower invertebrates such as Hydra, and is composed of a network of neurons. The neural system is better organized in insects, where a brain is present along with a number of gan

129221.subject: Zoology
129221.text: What is the difference in impulse transmission between electrical synapses and chemical synapses?
options: Impulse transmission across an electrical synapse is always slower than that across a chemical synapse
Impulse transmission across an electrical synapse is always faster than that across a chemical synapse
Impulse transmission across electrical and chemical synapses is the same
There is no difference in impulse transmission between electrical and chemical synapses
129221.sol: The action potential is generated in response to a stimulus and travels along the length of the axon, transmitting the nerve impulse. The rise in permeability to Na⁺ is short-lived and is followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺. K⁺ diffuses outside the membrane, restoring the resting potential of the membrane.A synapse is a junction between two neurons that allows the transmission of a nerve impulse from one neuron to another Electrical synapses are rare in our system. At electrical synapses, the membranes of pre-

129230.subject: Zoology
129230.text: What is the difference between transmission of an impulse across an electrical synapse and a chemical synapse?
options: Transmission across an electrical synapse is faster
Transmission across an electrical synapse involves neurotransmitters
Transmission across a chemical synapse is faster
Transmission across a chemical synapse involves neurotransmitters
129230.sol: The brain acts as the "command and control system" and controls various functions such as voluntary movements, balance, vital organs, circadian rhythms, endocrine glands and human behavior. The brain is divided into three major parts, the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain, which are the main regions that control different functions in the body.The cranial meninges consisting of dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater protect the brain and act as a protective layer. The outer layer of the cranial meninges is called the

129428.subject: Zoology
129428.text: 'Adaptation' of eyes in dark is due to
options: depletion of vision pigment in rods
depletion of vision pigment in cones
repletion of vision pigment in rods
repletion of vision pigment in cones
129428.sol: Two types of photoreceptor cells are present in retina, ie, rods and cones. (i) Rods: These cells are active in dark Rhodopsin, a vision pigment is present in rods. In strong light, rhodopsin is bleached due to splitting of its two components, ie, scotopsin and retinal. But is reformed in dim light, ie, dark. (ii) Cones: These cells are active in strong light. Iodopsin a pigment is present in cones. These cells produce hare coloured image in bright light.

129549.subject: Zoology
129549.text: What is the effect of ADH on blood vessels?
129549.sol: Osmoreceptors in the body are activated by changes in blood volume, body fluid volume and ionic concentration. An excessive loss of fluid from the body can activate these receptors which stimulate the hypothalamus to release antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or vasopressin from the neurohypophysis. ADH facilitates water reabsorption from latter parts of the tubule, thereby preventing diuresis. An increase in body fluid volume can switch off the osmoreceptors and suppress the ADH release to complete the feedback. ADH can a

129934.subject: Zoology
129934.text: Select the correct option mentioning the right feature of A,B,C,D or E.
options: During swallowing glottis can be covered by a thick elastic cartilaginous flap called A
C is a cartilaginous box which helps in sound production.
The thoracic chamber is formed on the lower side by the circular shaped E
B is called the sound box
129934.sol: B is Larynx which is also called the sound box and contains vocal cords. A is Epiglottis and is thin elastic cartilaginous flap not thick. E is Diaphragm and is dome shaped not circular shaped. C is Trachea and B is Larynx which is the sound box not C. Larynx is a cartilaginous box which helps in sound production and hence called the sound box. During swallowing glottis can be covered by a thin elastic cartilaginous flap called epiglottis to prevent the entry of food into the larynx. Trachea is a straight tube exte

130117.subject: Zoology
130117.text: Hiccups can be best described as
options: forceful contraction of intercostal muscles during deep breathing
vibration of the soft palate during breathing while sleeping
130117.sol: A hiccup can be described as a jerky incomplete inspiration. It is an involuntary contraction of the diaphragm that may repeat several times per minute. In medical terms, it is known as synchronous diaphragmatic flutter (SDF).

130416.subject: Zoology
130416.text: What type of joint is present between atlas and axis?
130416.sol: Pivot joint is present between atlas and axis.

130792.subject: Zoology
130792.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the biological basis and the legal status of amniocentesis in India?
options: It analyses the chromosomal pattern of foetal cells in the amniotic fluid and is legally permitted for detecti
It analyses maternal blood cells to detect genetic disorders and is completely banned in India for all purpose
It analyses the chromosomal pattern of foetal cells and is promoted as an RCH strategy to maintain a balanced
It analyses the dissolved substances in the amniotic fluid but is completely banned in India for all purposes
130792.sol: Amniocentesis involves taking some of the amniotic fluid of the developing foetus to analyse the foetal cells and dissolved substances. It is based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo. It is legally permitted and used to test for the presence of certain genetic disorders such as Down's syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anaemia. However, there is a statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticide. It is

130831.subject: Zoology
130831.text: What are the regions in the testis that contain immunologically competent cells?
130831.sol: Each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced. Each seminiferous tubule is lined on its inside by two types of cells called male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells. The male germ cells undergo meiotic divisions finally leading to sperm formation, while Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells. The regions outside the seminiferous tubules called interstitial spaces, contain small blood vessels and interstitial cells or Leydig cells. Leydig cells

130846.subject: Zoology
130846.text: What are the two zones present in the ovarian stroma?
130846.sol: The female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries along with a pair of oviducts, uterus, cervix, vagina and the external genitalia located in pelvic region. These parts of the system along with a pair of the mammary glands are integrated structurally and functionally to support the processes of ovulation, fertilisation, pregnancy, birth and child care. Ovaries are the primary female sex organs that produce the female gamete (ovum) and several steroid hormones (ovarian hormones). The ovaries are located o

131101.subject: Zoology
131101.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. At puberty only 60,000-80,000 primary follicles are left in each ovary. 2. The primary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca and are called secondary follicles. 3. The secondary follicle soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterised by a fluid filled cavity called ovum. 4. The theca layer is organise
131101.sol: At puberty only 60,000-80,000 primary follicles are left in each ovary. The primary follicles get surrounded by more layers of granulosa cells and a new theca and are called secondary follicles. The secondary follicle soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterised by a fluid filled cavity called antrum. The theca layer is organised into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa

131610.subject: Zoology
131610.text: What is polymorphism at the genetic level?
options: An abnormality in the DNA sequence
Variation in the DNA sequence due to mutations
A normal feature of the DNA sequence
131610.sol: As polymorphism in DNA sequence is the basis of genetic mapping of human genome as well as of DNA fingerprinting, it is essential that we understand what DNA polymorphism means in simple terms. Polymorphism (variation at genetic level) arises due to mutations . New mutations may arise in an individual either in somatic cells or in the germ cells (cells that generate gametes in sexually reproducing organisms). If a germ cell mutation does not seriously impair an individual's ability to have offspring who can transmi

131770.subject: Zoology
131770.text: Control of gene expression in prokaryotes takes place at the level of:
131770.sol: Control of gene expression in prokaryotes takes place at the level of transcription when the codons are being transcribed from DNA.

132308.text: What does the given figure represent?
options: Steps in making a cross in pea
Seven pairs of contrasting traits in pea plant studied by Mendel

132671.subject: Zoology
132671.text: What conclusion did Charles Darwin reach based on his observations during the voyage on H.M.S. Beagle?
options: Life forms were created as they are and have not changed
All life forms are exactly the same today as they were millions of years ago
Existing living forms share similarities with ancient life forms, and many life forms have become extinct
Evolution occurs instantaneously without gradual changes
132671.sol: Conventional religious literature tells us about the theory of special creation. This theory has three connotations. One, that all living organisms (species or types) that we see today were created as such. Two, that the diversity was always the same since creation and will be the same in future also. Three, that earth is about 4000 years old. All these ideas were strongly challenged during the nineteenth century. Based on observations made during a sea voyage in a sail ship called H.M.S. Beagle round the world, Ch

133040.subject: Zoology
133040.text: Which one of the following pairs of items correctly belongs to the category of organs mentioned against it?
options: Wings of honey-bee and wings of crow - Homologous organs
Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita - Analogous organs
Nictitating membrane and blind spot in human eye - Vestigial organs
Nephridia of earthworm and malpighian tubules of cockroach - Excretory organs
133040.sol: Wings of honey bee and the wings of crow are analogous. Thorn of Bougaivillea and tendrils of Cucurbita are homologous. Blind spot in humans represent the point where the optic nerve will leave the eye ball so it is not vestigeal.

133330.subject: Zoology
133330.text: Identify the site where Wuchereria bancrofti is normally found on the human body?
133330.sol: Wuchereria (W. bancrofti and W. malayi), the filarial worms cause a slowly developing chronic inflammation of the organs in which they live for many years, usually the lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs and the disease is called elephantiasis or filariasis (Figure 8.2). The genital organs are also often affected, resulting in gross deformities. The pathogens are transmitted to a healthy person through the bite by the female mosquito vectors

133995.subject: Zoology
133995.text: Assertion : Saccharomyces cerevisiae produces acetic acid. Reason : Trichoderma polysporum produces blood cholestrol lowering agent.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false

134249.sol: Some strains of Bacillus thuringiensis produce proteins that kill certain insects such as lepidopterans (tobacco budworm, armyworm), coleopterans (beetles) and dipterans (flies, mosquitoes)

134293.subject: Zoology
134293.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Bacillus thuringiensis strains do not kill themselves despite producing insecticidal protein crystals. Reason (R): The Bt toxin protein exists as an inactive protoxin that requires an acidic pH, which is only found in the insect gut, to become active. In the light of the above statements, choose th
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.
134293.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because the Bt toxin protein exists as an inactive protoxin in the bacteria, which is why it does not kill the Bacillus thuringiensis strains that produce it. Reason (R) is incorrect because the inactive protoxin requires an alkaline pH, not an acidic pH, to become active. The alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilises the protein crystals, converting them into the active toxin. Therefore, Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct. Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.

134439.subject: Zoology
134439.text: What is the specific base sequence recognized by Hind II?
134439.sol: The first restriction endonuclease–Hind II, whose functioning depended on a specific DNA nucleotide sequence was isolated and characterized five years later. It was found that Hind II always cut DNA molecules at a particular point by recognizing a specific sequence of six base pairs . This specific base sequence is known as the recognition sequence for Hind II. Besides Hind II, today we know more than 900 restriction enzymes that have been isolated from over 230 strains of bacteria each of which recognize different

134771.subject: Zoology
134771.text: A researcher sets up a standard Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) to amplify a gene of interest. However, instead of adding Taq polymerase, they mistakenly add ordinary DNA polymerase isolated from Escherichia coli . All other components (template DNA, primers, and dNTPs) are correctly added. What will be the most likely consequence on the gene amplification process?
options: Amplification will occur but at a much slower rate.
The primers will fail to anneal to the template DNA.
No amplification will occur as the enzyme will be denatured during the first cycle.
Continuous amplification will occur but with a high rate of mutations.
134771.sol: PCR involves three main steps: Denaturation, Annealing, and Extension. The denaturation step requires a high temperature (around 94^ C ) to separate the double-stranded template DNA. Ordinary DNA polymerase from E. coli is not thermostable. It will be denatured and permanently destroyed during the very first high-temperature denaturation step. Consequently, no extension of primers can occur, resulting in no amplification of the gene. This is why Taq polymerase, isolated from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquat

134812.subject: Zoology
134812.text: A researcher prepares a standard Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) mixture but mistakenly adds normal human DNA polymerase instead of Taq polymerase isolated from Thermus aquaticus. The mixture is then subjected to a standard thermal cycle: 94^ C for 1 minute, 55^ C for 45 seconds, and 72^ C for 1 minute. Which specific step of the first PCR cycle will fail to produce its intended molecular outcome?
134812.sol: The first step of the PCR cycle is denaturation at 94^ C , which relies solely on heat to break the hydrogen bonds between DNA strands. This step will occur successfully. However, normal human DNA polymerase is not thermostable and will be irreversibly denatured (destroyed) by this high temperature. The second step, annealing at 55^ C , also occurs successfully because primers hybridize to the template DNA based on complementary base pairing, which does not require an enzyme. The third step, extension at 72^ C , re

134861.subject: Zoology
134861.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): PCR is routinely used to detect mutations in genes in suspected cancer patients. Reason (R): PCR can amplify specific DNA segments, allowing the detection of mutated genes even when the number of affected cells is very low. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the op
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
134861.sol: Assertion (A) is true. According to NCERT, PCR is a powerful technique routinely used to detect mutations in genes in suspected cancer patients. Reason (R) is also true and provides the correct explanation for the assertion. The primary diagnostic power of PCR lies in its ability to amplify very low amounts of nucleic acids. Even if the number of mutated cells is extremely low (as in the early stages of cancer before large masses form), PCR can amplify the specific mutated DNA segments to detectable levels, making

134928.subject: Zoology
134928.text: Which of the following can act as molecular scissors?
134928.sol: Option (3) is the correct answer because the cutting of DNA at specific location became possible with the use of restriction enzymes. So, they are also called molecular scissors. The DNA fragments can be joined together by using DNA ligase. They are called molecular glue. DNA polymerase helps in the extension step of PCR.

134954.subject: Zoology
134954.text: In Recombinant DNA technology antibiotics are used: *Note: There was ambiguity in options in the original paper, hence the options are changed.
134954.sol: Selectable marker: Helps in identifying and eliminating non-transformants and selectively permitting the growth of the transformants. Normally, the genes encoding resistance to antibiotics such as ampicillin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline or kanamycin, etc., are considered useful selectable markers for E.coli. During the screening, it helps in differentiating the cells that have alien DNA or gene of interest.

6a16f3267cfacf7984f866f0.subject: Chemistry
6a16f3267cfacf7984f866f0.text: Unlike transition metal complexes, the colors of lanthanoid(III) complexes are generally not affected by the nature of the ligands. The primary reason for this behavior is that:
options: the 4f orbitals are deeply buried and effectively shielded by 5s and 5p electrons.
the energy difference between 4f and 5d orbitals is very small, allowing rapid electron exchange.
lanthanoids do not undergo f-f transitions in the presence of strong field ligands.
the 4f electrons are strongly repelled by the ligands, preventing any interaction.
6a16f3267cfacf7984f866f0.sol: The colors of lanthanoid(III) complexes arise mainly from f-f transitions. The 4f orbitals in lanthanoids are deeply buried inside the atom and are effectively shielded from the external environment by the filled 5s and 5p orbitals. Due to this shielding, the 4f electrons do not interact significantly with the ligands. Consequently, the crystal field splitting of the 4f orbitals is very small, and the energy levels of the 4f orbitals are largely unaffected by the nature of the ligands. Thus, the colors of lanthanoi

6a252ff098efbb6c17e929aa.subject: Chemistry
6a252ff098efbb6c17e929aa.text: Observe the given figure showing the boundary surface diagrams of four different atomic orbitals labeled P, Q, R, and S. Match the orbital shapes in List I with their corresponding designations and azimuthal quantum numbers in List II. List I List II A Shape P 1 p_x orbital, l = 1 B Shape Q 2 d_ z^2 orbital, l = 2 C Shape R 3 s orbital, l = 0 D Shape S 4 d_ xz orbital, l = 2 Choose the correct answer from the options
6a252ff098efbb6c17e929aa.sol: Shape P is spherically symmetric, which corresponds to an s orbital. For an s orbital, the azimuthal quantum number is l = 0 . Thus, A matches with 3. Shape Q has two lobes oriented along the x-axis, which corresponds to a p_x orbital. For a p orbital, l = 1 . Thus, B matches with 1. Shape R has four lobes lying in the xz plane between the x and z axes, which corresponds to a d_ xz orbital. For a d orbital, l = 2 . Thus, C matches with 4. Shape S has two lobes along the z-axis and a donut-shaped ring in the xy plan

6a252ff198efbb6c17e929b6.subject: Chemistry
6a252ff198efbb6c17e929b6.text: The given compound is to be reduced to its corresponding primary amine. Which of the following reagent mixtures is preferred for this conversion in industrial processes because the acid is regenerated during the reaction?
options: H₂ gas in the presence of finely divided Ni
6a252ff198efbb6c17e929b6.sol: Reduction of nitro compounds to primary amines can be carried out using metal-acid mixtures such as Sn / HCl or Fe / HCl . In industrial processes, the use of iron scrap ( Fe ) and hydrochloric acid ( HCl ) is preferred over Sn / HCl . This is because the FeCl₂ formed during the reaction gets hydrolysed to release hydrochloric acid back into the reaction mixture: FeCl₂ + 2 H₂O Fe(OH)₂ + 2 HCl Thus, only a small amount of HCl is required to initiate the reaction, making the process highly cost-effective. Answer: Fe

6a0e277a165ae1327797b3e5.subject: Biology
6a0e277a165ae1327797b3e5.text: Read the following statements regarding Plant Growth Regulators (PGRs): (A) Gibberellins promote bolting in beet, cabbages and many plants with a rosette habit. (B) Ethylene delays the senescence and abscission of leaves and flowers. (C) Cytokinins help in overcoming apical dominance. (D) Abscisic acid acts as an antagonist to GAs in most situations. (E) 2,4-D is widely used to kill mature monocotyledonous weeds. Sel
6a0e277a165ae1327797b3e5.sol: Statement (A) is correct as gibberellins promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages, and many plants with a rosette habit. Statement (B) is incorrect because ethylene promotes senescence and abscission of plant organs, especially leaves and flowers. Statement (C) is correct as cytokinins promote lateral shoot growth and help overcome apical dominance. Statement (D) is correct because abscisic acid (ABA) generally acts as an antagonist to gibberellins (GAs), for example, in seed

6a0e277a165ae1327797b3fe.subject: Biology
6a0e277a165ae1327797b3fe.text: Read the following statements regarding the structure of a mature human sperm and select the incorrect one.
options: The middle piece possesses numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for the movement of the tail.
The acrosome is a cap-like structure filled with enzymes that help in fertilization of the ovum.
The sperm head contains an elongated diploid nucleus that carries the genetic material.
The tail facilitates sperm motility which is essential for fertilization.
6a0e277a165ae1327797b3fe.sol: A mature human sperm is a haploid male gamete. It consists of a head, neck, middle piece, and tail. The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, not a diploid nucleus. The anterior portion of this nucleus is covered by a cap-like structure called the acrosome, which contains enzymes that help in the fertilization of the ovum. The middle piece contains numerous mitochondria, which provide energy for the movement of the tail, facilitating sperm motility essential for fertilization. Therefore, the statement t

6a13e468688ac6d0667aad53.subject: Biology
6a13e468688ac6d0667aad53.text: In which of the following pairs of plants do the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on its peripheral part?
6a13e468688ac6d0667aad53.sol: In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on its peripheral part. The ovary is initially one-chambered but becomes two-chambered due to the formation of a false septum. Mustard and Argemone are examples of plants that exhibit parietal placentation. Dianthus and Primrose exhibit free central placentation. Sunflower and Marigold exhibit basal placentation. Tomato and Lemon exhibit axile placentation. Answer: Mustard and Argemone

6a1bb6be107bf677676d9f5b.subject: Chemistry
6a1bb6be107bf677676d9f5b.text: Match List I with List II. 6a1bb6be107bf677676d9f5b.sol: Semicarbazone is formed when a carbonyl compound reacts with semicarbazide ( NH₂NHCONH₂ ). Thus, A matches with 4. 306426.subject: Physics
306426.text: A thin metal plate P is inserted between the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor having capacitance C such that its edges make contact with both plates, as shown in the figure. The new capacitance becomes
306426.sol: When the thin metal plate P is inserted such that its edges make contact with both plates of the capacitor, it effectively short-circuits the two plates. Because the plates are connected by a conducting material, the potential difference V between them becomes zero for any finite charge. The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as C = Q V . Substituting V = 0 , the new capacitance becomes C' = Q 0 . Therefore, the new capacitance is infinite.

306409.subject: Physics
306409.text: The water equivalent of a body is expressed in
306409.sol: The water equivalent of a body is defined as the mass of water which requires the same amount of heat as the body for the same rise in temperature. Since it represents the mass of water, its unit is the same as that of mass. Therefore, the water equivalent of a body is expressed in kg .
